title: Open/closed recollement for condensed coefficient modules
statement: Use [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] with complementary open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ assumed quasi-compact as a morphism (for every affine open $W\subseteq X$, the intersection $U\cap W$ is quasi-compact), and let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring sheaf on profinite sets with the finite jointly surjective topology. Put $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ for $T=X,U,Z$ using [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category], and write $D^+(T,\Lambda)$ for complexes of $\Lambda_T$-module sheaves with cohomology zero in all sufficiently negative degrees in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. On these categories there are adjunctions $j_!\dashv j^*\dashv Rj_*$ and $i^*\dashv i_*\dashv Ri^!$, natural in their arguments. The functors $j^*,j_!,i^*,i_*$ come from exact functors on module sheaves. The pullbacks $j^*,i^*$ preserve all small colimits of sheaves; $i_*$ is fully faithful and $i^*i_*\cong\mathrm{id}$. The functor $Ri^!$ is left t-exact: $K\in D^{\geq a}(X,\Lambda)$ implies $Ri^!K\in D^{\geq a}(Z,\Lambda)$. There are natural distinguished triangles $j_!j^*K\to K\to i_*i^*K\to j_!j^*K[1]$ and $i_*Ri^!K\to K\to Rj_*j^*K\to i_*Ri^!K[1]$, with maps given by the units and counits of these adjunctions. The functors, triangles and adjunction bijections commute with shifts. Functorial bounded-below injective-resolution models may be used for the right derived functors, with common lower bound $a$ when their inputs have this bound.

proof.text: Set $R=\Lambda_X$. The monoidal composition comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-point-pullback], evaluated at the arbitrary condensed ring $\Lambda$, identify $i^{-1}R\cong\Lambda_Z$ and $j^{-1}R\cong\Lambda_U$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] to $R$: it gives the sheaf short exact sequence, exact $i_*$, $i^*i_*\cong\mathrm{id}$ and $j^*i_*=0$. The operations adjunction $i^*\dashv i_*$ and its invertible counit imply full faithfulness of $i_*$. Part (1) of [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] identifies $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with $X_{\mathrm{proet}}/U$; its topological identification restricts any ring sheaf $R$, without using the constant-ring clauses (2)-(3). Hence [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] supplies exact $j_!$ and $j_!\dashv j^*$. The operations input gives exact $i^*,j^*$ and their direct-image adjunctions. Finally, for every $V\to U$, $(j^*j_*G)(V)=G(U\times_X V)=G(V)$, since $j$ is a monomorphism; these identifications are the open counit and commute with restrictions and the $R_U$-action. Thus $j^*j_*\to\mathrm{id}$ is an isomorphism. No constant or discrete coefficient identification is made.

proof.text: Construct the sheaf exceptional inverse image instead of assuming it: put $S(F)=\ker(F\to j_*j^*F)$ and $i^!F=i^*S(F)$. Exact $j^*$ and $j^*j_*\cong\mathrm{id}$ give $j^*S(F)=0$, so the sheaf short exact sequence gives $S(F)\cong i_*i^*S(F)$. For a sheaf $G$ on $Z$, $\operatorname{Hom}(i_*G,j_*j^*F)=\operatorname{Hom}(j^*i_*G,j^*F)=0$. Thus every map $i_*G\to F$ factors uniquely through $S(F)$. Full faithfulness of $i_*$ identifies these factors with maps $G\to i^!F$, naturally. This proves $i_*\dashv i^!$. In particular $i^!$ is additive and left exact. It preserves injectives: an extension problem into $i^!I$ is, by adjunction, one into $I$ along $i_*$ of a monomorphism, which is monic by exactness.

source.place: (3.3); sheaf kernel construction underlying the closed right adjoint

proof.text: The small-site module categories are Grothendieck by the ringed-site resolution theorem. Their functorial injective embeddings and the generic bounded-resolution input give functorial resolutions $K\to I(K)$ whose terms vanish below every lower bound of $K$. Bounded-below injective complexes are K-injective. An object cohomologically in degrees $\geq a$ has a representative with injective terms zero below $a$, by the prescribed-bound representative theorem; thus a diagram of representing complexes with this common cohomological bound can first be replaced, naturally in its chain maps, by the canonical good truncation $\tau_{\geq a}$ and then resolved by the same functor. This supplies common-bound models without taking an unbounded replacement and assuming it preserves bounds. Explicitly, the common-bound truncation $T_aK$ has terms zero for $n<a$, $\operatorname{coker}(d_K^{a-1})$ for $n=a$, and $K^n$ for $n>a$, with the induced differential at $a$. The quotient maps define a chain map $K\to T_aK$, natural in chain maps. The formula $H^n=\ker d^n/\operatorname{im}d^{n-1}$ shows that this map preserves $H^n$ for $n\geq a$; its target has zero cohomology below $a$, so it is a quasi-isomorphism when $H^n(K)=0$ there. This proves the asserted functorial common-bound replacement directly.

source.place: Stacks bounded-below resolutions; functorial common-bound models

proof.text: Apply exact derived factorization to $j_!,j^*,i^*,i_*$. The K-injective total-derived theorem constructs $Ri^!$ from the additive sheaf functor in step 2; the operations input constructs $Rj_*$. All are everywhere defined on the unbounded derived categories since module sheaves have K-injective resolutions, and restrict to $D^+$ using step 3. The general derived-adjunction theorem applied to each sheaf adjunction gives $j_!\dashv j^*\dashv Rj_*$ and $i^*\dashv i_*\dashv Ri^!$. Its exact-functor hypotheses hold by step 1. On a resolution zero below $a$, both $j_*I$ and $i^!I$ vanish below $a$, so $Rj_*$ and $Ri^!$ preserve $D^{\geq a}$. In particular the latter is left t-exact. The sheaf identity $i^*i_*\cong\mathrm{id}$ remains an identity of exact termwise derived functors, so $i_*$ remains fully faithful.

Represent $K$ by a bounded-below complex. Apply the sheaf sequence of step 1 in each degree; naturality makes its three terms complexes and its arrows chain maps. The existing generic complex-SES triangle lemma gives the distinguished triangle $j_!j^*K\to K\to i_*i^*K\to j_!j^*K[1]$. Exact derived factorization identifies its terms with the stated functors, without resolutions. Its first two maps are exactly the sheaf counit and unit localized, hence the derived counit and unit. The generic lemma also gives naturality under maps of these sequences.

For the second triangle choose the functorial bounded-below injective model $I=I(K)$. Since $j^*$ is right adjoint to exact $j_!$, it preserves K-injectives; since $j_*$ is right adjoint to exact $j^*$ it does too. Thus $j_*j^*I$ computes $Rj_*j^*K$, with unit represented by the actual chain map $u:I\to j_*j^*I$. Form the explicit complex $L=\operatorname{Cone}(u)[-1]$ and its rotated cone triangle $L\to I\to j_*j^*I\to L[1]$. Applying exact $j^*$ gives the cone of an isomorphism (the restriction of $u$ is inverse to the open counit). That cone is contractible, so $j^*L=0$ in the derived category. Apply the first triangle, already proved, to $L$: its first term vanishes, and the unit $L\to i_*i^*L$ is an isomorphism. Notice $L^n$ is a direct sum of $I^n$ and $(j_*j^*I)^{n-1}$, so it is zero for $n<a$ whenever $I$ is.

source.place: (3.3)-(3.4); explicit fibre of the open unit

proof.text: Write $A=i^*L$ and identify $L$ with $i_*A$ by the unit of step 6. For any $B\in D^+(Z,\Lambda)$ and any integer $n$, derived adjunction and $j^*i_*=0$ give $\operatorname{Hom}(i_*B,Rj_*j^*K[n])=0$. Apply exactness of Hom into the cone triangle and its inverse rotation: the vanishing for $n=0,-1$ makes $\operatorname{Hom}(i_*B,L)\to\operatorname{Hom}(i_*B,K)$ a bijection. Full faithfulness of $i_*$ makes this $\operatorname{Hom}(B,A)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(i_*B,K)$, naturally in $B$. Hence $A$ represents the same functor as $Ri^!K$ from step 4. The canonical representing isomorphism identifies $i_*A\to K$ with its counit (both correspond to the identity of the right-adjoint object). Replacing $L$ by $i_*Ri^!K$ in the cone triangle proves the second asserted triangle, including its maps.

source.place: (3.3); identify the fibre by its adjunction, rather than posit a fibre-identification input

proof.text: The cone construction on the functorial models is natural in chain maps. Quasi-isomorphisms between their K-injective replacements are homotopy equivalences; the additive functors $j^*,j_*$ preserve those equivalences, so their localized maps are isomorphisms. The concrete cone maps are morphisms of distinguished triangles with those two isomorphisms; the generic triangle-morphism isomorphism lemma makes the third map an isomorphism too. The triangle therefore descends naturally to the derived category; the representing identification in step 7 is natural in $K$ as well. Exact termwise functors commute with shifts by the identity on the shifted components. For right derived functors, resolution comparison gives the shift isomorphisms by the generic derived-triangulated theorem; the Hom bijections arise from the termwise adjunction, which commutes with simultaneous shifts, so these comparisons commute with units and counits. The two triangles commute with shifts with the standard cone/rotated-triangle signs; no choice of arbitrary cones in a triangulated category is being asserted to be functorial.

source.place: (3.3)-(3.4); naturality and shift comparisons of the concrete models

proof.text: Finally the sheaf pullbacks preserve small colimits directly from their adjunctions: maps from $j^*(\operatorname{colim}F_d)$ to $G$ are maps from $\operatorname{colim}F_d$ to $j_*G$, hence compatible families of maps $j^*F_d\to G$; the identical calculation with $i_*$ proves the claim for $i^*$. Colimits here exist in the small-site module categories. Step 3 gives common-bound functorial injective models for both right derived functors, while step 4 shows their images still have the same bound. All clauses of the statement now hold.
